name: MD-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans 12 points Democratic, anchoring the race firmly on the incumbent's side
Elfreth holds a roughly 90-to-1 fundraising advantage ($1.14M raised vs. $12.7K)
Challenger Flowers has only about $2,000 cash on hand, limiting any ability to compete
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95 percent
model.rationale: The district's twelve-point Democratic lean, the incumbent's overwhelming financial edge, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win around 95 percent all point the same direction, and no polls or expert ratings suggest the general election is competitive.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending for Flowers or an unforeseen incumbent stumble could narrow the margin, though nothing currently signals competitive risk.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's third district sits well inside Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of twelve points toward Democrats. First-term incumbent Sarah Elfreth is seeking re-election and has built a substantial financial advantage, raising about $1.1 million with $336,000 on hand. Republican Berney Flowers has raised roughly $13,000 and reports about $2,000 in cash, leaving him little capacity for advertising or outreach.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win around 95 percent. The combination of the district's lean, incumbency, and lopsided fundraising points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with little evidence of a competitive general election taking shape.
